en: to reduce; to cut; to bring down

examples.en: The store is cutting its prices.
The bank lowered the interest rate.
If you lower the price, customers increase.
They are looking for ways to cut taxes.
They plan to lower the fee.
We are selling at the reduced price.

explain: 가격, 이자, 세금 같은 숫자를 내릴 때 써요. 반대말은 '인상하다'예요. '값을 내리다'보다 격식 있는 말이에요.

phrases.en: Bus fares will be reduced from next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 내렸는지보다 값이 내려진 결과가 중요할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the result of the price being lowered matters more than who lowered it.

phrases.example: 이번 주에 가격 인하 행사를 해요.
phrases.en: There is a price cut event this week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '인하'를 붙여 광고나 안내문에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun form often seen in ads and notices.

phrases.en: The company decided to reduce the fee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인하하기로 결정했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means that someone has decided to make a cut.

explain_en: Use it when lowering numbers like prices, interest, or taxes. The opposite is '인상하다'. It is more formal than '값을 내리다'.

gh: formal; make amounts or levels drop

p.n: Prices are lowered, so 줄이다 is unnatural here.

t90.ax: They plan to lower the fee.

examples.ko: 이번 달에는 잉여 자금이 조금 생겼어요.
examples.en: This month some surplus funds came up.

examples.ko: 회사의 잉여 인력을 다른 부서로 옮겼어요.
examples.en: The company moved its surplus staff to another department.
Surplus farm products are sometimes sold at a low price.
I saved the surplus that was left over after spending.

examples.ko: 잉여가 생기지 않도록 주문량을 잘 맞춰요.
examples.en: We adjust the order amount well so that no excess builds up.

examples.ko: 잉여 예산은 다음 달로 넘기기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to carry the excess budget over to next month.

explain: 필요한 만큼 쓰고도 남은 것을 말해요. '나머지'나 '남은 것'은 일상 말이고, '잉여'는 경제·회사 글에서 '잉여 인력', '잉여 생산물'처럼 써요. 인터넷에서는 할 일 없는 사람을 놀리는 말로도 쓰니 조심하세요.

phrases.en: They sold the surplus crops cheaply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요한 만큼 쓰고도 남은 농산물을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to farm products left over after meeting demand.

phrases.en: We carried the surplus funds over to next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사나 단체가 쓰고 남은 돈을 부르는 회계 쪽 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An accounting term for money left over after spending.

phrases.en: We store the surplus power and use it later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓰고 남은 전기를 말할 때 쓰는 기술·경제 쪽 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A technical/economic collocation for leftover electricity.

explain_en: It refers to what is left over after using what was needed. 나머지 and 남은 것 are everyday words, while 잉여 appears in economic and business writing, as in 잉여 인력 and 잉여 생산물. Online it is also used to tease someone with nothing to do, so be careful.

t90.ax: This month some surplus funds came up.

en: as much as; no less than

examples.ko: 그 책은 자그마치 천 쪽이나 돼요.
examples.en: That book is no less than a thousand pages.

examples.ko: 오늘 모인 사람이 자그마치 오천 명이래요.
examples.en: They say as many as five thousand people gathered today.
This bag costs a whopping three million won.

examples.ko: 그는 혼자서 자그마치 열 시간을 걸었어요.
examples.en: He walked for a full ten hours all by himself.

examples.ko: 시험 준비에 자그마치 일 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Preparing for the exam took a whole year.

examples.ko: 이 나무는 자그마치 오백 살이 넘었어요.
examples.en: This tree is over five hundred years old, no less.

explain: 수나 양, 시간이 생각보다 많아서 놀랍다는 느낌을 강조할 때 써요. 뒤에는 숫자나 단위가 오고 '고작'과는 반대의 느낌이에요. '자그마하다(작다)'와 모양이 비슷하지만 뜻은 반대라서 헷갈리지 않게 조심하세요.

phrases.example: 이 일을 하는 데 자그마치 십 년이나 걸렸어요.
phrases.en: It took no less than ten years to do this.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자그마치' 뒤에 숫자와 '이나'를 붙이면 놀라움이 더 잘 드러나요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding a number and 이나 after it brings out the surprise.

phrases.example: 올해 가격이 자그마치 두 배가 됐어요.
phrases.en: This year the price doubled, no less.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 늘어난 정도를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to stress a large increase.

phrases.en: As many as a thousand people came to the venue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 수가 예상보다 많아서 놀랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the number of people is surprisingly large.
phrases.en_equiv: as many as a thousand people

explain_en: It stresses surprise that a number, amount or length of time is larger than expected, and is followed by a number or unit. It feels like the opposite of '고작' (a mere). It looks like '자그마하다' (small), but the meaning is the reverse, so be careful not to mix them up.

t90.ax: Preparing for the exam took a whole year.

examples.ko: 작은 가게를 열 자본금을 모으고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm saving up the capital to open a small shop.

examples.ko: 회사를 만들 때 자본금이 얼마나 필요해요?
examples.en: How much capital do you need to start a company?
We didn't have enough capital, so we decided to take investment.
That company's capital is fifty million won.
I invested with a friend to increase the capital.
It's hard to start a business without capital.

explain: 가게를 열 때 쓰는 돈은 일상에서 '창업 자금'이나 '밑천'이라고 해요. 회사를 세울 때 법적으로 등록하는 돈일 때 '자본금'이라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I borrowed startup funds from the bank.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가게나 사업을 시작할 때 쓰는 돈을 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday way to talk about money for starting a shop or business.

phrases.en: I need a little money to start my business.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자본금'보다 쉽고 편한 말로, 무언가를 시작하는 데 드는 돈을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plainer, more casual word than 자본금 for the money needed to get started.

phrases.en: I couldn't open the shop because I lacked capital.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자본금'과 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 말이에요. 돈이 모자랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A very common pairing with 자본금 when the money is not enough.

explain_en: Everyday talk calls money for opening a shop '창업 자금' or '밑천'. '자본금' is used for the money legally registered when a company is founded.

t90.ax: That company's capital is fifty million won.

en: rich man; man of property; man of fortune

examples.en: He is a wealthy man who made money from real estate.
Wealthy people get investment advice separately.

examples.ko: 한 자산가가 학교에 큰 기부금을 냈어요.
examples.en: A wealthy man donated a large sum to the school.
I am not wealthy, but I save diligently.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 자산가를 위한 세금 이야기가 나왔어요.
examples.en: The news had a story about taxes for the wealthy.
I heard he grew up without worries as a rich man's son.

explain: '부자'가 일상에서 가장 흔하고, '자산가'는 땅, 건물, 주식처럼 재산이 많은 사람을 말할 때 조금 격식 있게 써요. 뉴스나 금융 이야기에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.example: 저 건물 주인은 아주 큰 부자예요.
phrases.en: The owner of that building is very rich.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 가장 흔한 말이고, '자산가'보다 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common everyday word, more casual than '자산가'.

phrases.en: He became a man of wealth through stock investing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재산이 많은 사람이 되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means becoming a person with substantial assets.

phrases.example: 젊은 자산가들이 새로운 투자 방법을 찾고 있어요.
phrases.en: Young wealthy people are looking for new ways to invest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 경제 기사에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often found in news and economic articles.

explain_en: '부자' is the everyday word; '자산가' sounds a bit more formal and fits people with lots of property, buildings or stocks. You often hear it in news and finance talk.

en: to be low; to be low-pitched

examples.ko: 올해 우리 가게의 판매 실적이 저조해요.
examples.en: Our shop's sales results are poor this year.
Turnout for the event was far too low.
I worry when my exam scores are poor.

examples.ko: 요즘 우리 팀의 득점이 저조한 편이에요.
examples.en: Our team's scoring has been sluggish lately.
The response was weak, so we scaled down the event.

examples.ko: 출석이 저조하지 않도록 신경 써 주세요.
examples.en: Please make sure attendance doesn't turn out low.

explain: 성적, 실적, 참여율처럼 숫자로 보이는 결과가 기대보다 낮을 때 써요. 사람 자체를 가리키지 않고 '참여가 저조하다'처럼 일의 결과를 말해요. '부진하다'와 비슷한 상황에서 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: The player is worried because of the poor results.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대보다 낮은 성적이나 결과를 앞에서 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes results that are lower than expected.

phrases.en: This month's sales are not low.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대만큼 나쁘지 않다고 부정으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form, saying that results are not as low as feared.

phrases.en: Participation is low, so we are preparing the event again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과가 낮은 이유를 말하면서 다음 이야기를 이어 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives low results as the reason for what comes next.

explain_en: Used when a measurable result such as grades, performance, or turnout is lower than hoped. It describes the outcome of something, as in '참여가 저조하다', not a person. It's used in situations similar to 부진하다.

t90.ax: I worry when my exam scores are poor.

examples.ko: 검사에서 걸린 불량 제품은 전량 폐기했어요.
examples.en: All the defective products found in the inspection were discarded.

examples.ko: 주문한 물건 전량이 오늘 아침에 도착했어요.
examples.en: The whole amount of the goods I ordered arrived this morning.

examples.ko: 손님이 남은 빵 전량을 사 가셨어요.
examples.en: A customer bought all of the remaining bread.
We'll sell all of the stock at a discount starting tomorrow.

examples.ko: 전량으로 계약하면 가격을 더 깎아 준대요.
examples.en: They say they'll lower the price more if you contract for the whole amount.

examples.ko: 이번에 수확한 쌀은 전량 수출될 예정이에요.
examples.en: All of the rice harvested this time is going to be exported.

explain: '전량 폐기', '전량 수입', '전량 판매'처럼 물건의 양 전체를 말하는 업무·뉴스 말투예요. 일상에서는 '전부', '다', '몽땅'이라고 해요. 사람이나 시간에는 쓰지 않고 물건의 양에만 써요.

phrases.en: This fruit is all imported.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 물건을 전부 다른 나라에서 들여올 때 쓰는 업무·뉴스 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A business or news phrase for when an item is brought in entirely from abroad.

phrases.en: They recalled all of the defective products.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제 있는 물건을 모두 거두어들일 때 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in the news when all problem items are taken back.

phrases.en: All the items I ordered have arrived.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전량'은 딱딱하고, 일상에서는 '전부'나 '다'를 더 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '전량' is formal; in daily life '전부' or '다' sounds more natural.

explain_en: It is a business and news style word for the whole quantity of goods, as in '전량 폐기', '전량 수입' and '전량 판매'. In daily talk people say '전부', '다' or '몽땅'. It is not used for people or time, only for quantities of things.

en: to be reduced; to be cut

examples.en: Thanks to the new system, costs go down.
The electricity bill went down a lot.

examples.ko: 시간이 절감되면 다른 일도 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If time is saved, we can do other things too.

examples.ko: 인건비가 절감된 만큼 서비스를 좋게 만들었어요.
examples.en: We improved the service by as much as labor costs were cut.
Material costs are down and the quality is the same.
I expect the costs to come down.

explain: 비용·시간·에너지처럼 줄이고 싶은 것이 줄어들 때 써요. 일부러 줄이는 쪽은 '절감하다', 그 결과로 줄어든 쪽은 '절감되다'예요. 사람이 느끼는 감정에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: We bought new equipment with the money we saved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄어든 결과로 남은 돈을 말할 때 명사 앞에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun for money saved as a result of cutting costs.

phrases.en: The electricity bill went down a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이고 어떤 것에든 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday word that works for almost anything.

phrases.en: The energy-saving effect is very large.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄어든 정도를 이야기할 때 뉴스나 광고에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news and ads to talk about how much was saved.

explain_en: Used when costs, time or energy that you want to reduce actually go down. 절감하다 is cutting on purpose; 절감되다 is the result of being cut. It is not used for feelings.

gh: numbers or amounts simply go down

p.n: 감소되다 is a neutral decrease; 절감되다 implies saving on purpose.

t90.ax: I expect the costs to come down.

examples.ko: 이 영화의 제작비는 백억 원이 넘어요.
examples.en: This film's production cost is over ten billion won.
We postponed filming because the budget fell short.

examples.ko: 제작비를 줄이려고 장면을 몇 개 뺐어요.
examples.en: To cut production costs, they removed a few scenes.

examples.ko: 광고 영상 제작비를 먼저 알아보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm first checking how much an ad video would cost to make.

examples.ko: 적은 제작비로도 좋은 작품을 만들 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can make a good work even on a small budget.
I heard season 2 was canceled because of the production cost.

explain: 영화, 드라마, 영상, 책처럼 작품을 만드는 데 드는 돈에 써요. 공장에서 물건을 만드는 돈은 '생산비'나 '원가'를 더 많이 써요. '제작비를 들이다', '제작비가 들다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: This video cost a lot to produce.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만드는 데 돈이 쓰였다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say that making it took money.

phrases.en: To cut production costs, we filmed with a small team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 아끼려는 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when talking about plans to save money.

phrases.en: We got sponsorship to raise the money for the film.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요한 돈을 구할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you secure the money needed.

explain_en: It is used for the money spent making a work such as a film, drama, video, or book. For the cost of making goods in a factory, '생산비' or '원가' is more common. Common phrases are '제작비를 들이다' (spend production money) and '제작비가 들다' (production costs arise).

examples.ko: 월급에서 세금을 제하면 얼마 안 남아요.
examples.en: If you subtract tax from my salary, there isn't much left.

examples.ko: 식비를 제하고 나니 용돈이 거의 없어요.
examples.en: After deducting food costs, I have almost no spending money.
The amount with the fee taken out was deposited into my account.
I paid after deducting the points from the total.

examples.ko: 휴일을 제해도 일할 날이 스무 날은 돼요.
examples.en: Even after removing the holidays, there are twenty working days.
Please deduct the discount when you calculate.

explain: '빼다'와 같은 뜻인데 계산이나 돈 이야기에서 쓰는 글 같은 말이에요. 말로는 '빼다'나 '제외하다'를 더 많이 써요. '제한 금액'의 '제한'은 '뺀'이라는 뜻이라서 '제한(limit)'과 달라요.

phrases.example: 월급에서 월세를 빼면 남는 돈이 적어요.
phrases.en: If I subtract the rent from my salary, there's little money left.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제하다와 같은 뜻이고 말할 때 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 제하다 and much more natural when speaking.

phrases.example: 교통비를 제하고 나면 얼마 안 남아요.
phrases.en: After subtracting transportation costs, there isn't much left.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계산한 뒤의 결과를 말할 때 쓰는 연결 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form used to talk about the result after calculating.

phrases.en: Excluding tax, the salary is 3 million won.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계산에서 뺀다는 뜻으로 제하다보다 더 넓게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means leaving something out of a calculation, used more broadly than 제하다.

explain_en: It means the same as '빼다' (to subtract), but is a bookish word used in calculations and money talk; in speech people say '빼다' or '제외하다' more. In '제한 금액', '제한' means 'subtracted', which is different from '제한' meaning 'limit'.

examples.en: A few coins fell out of my wallet.

examples.ko: 이 자판기는 오백 원짜리 주화만 받아요.
examples.en: This vending machine only accepts 500-won coins.
I saw a very old coin at the museum.

examples.ko: 새 주화가 올해부터 나온다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that a new coin will come out starting this year.

examples.ko: 죄송하지만 지폐를 주화로 바꿔 주실 수 있어요?
examples.en: Sorry, but could you change this bill into coins?

examples.ko: 이 주화는 한쪽 면에 학이 그려져 있어요.
examples.en: This coin has a crane drawn on one side.

explain: 일상에서는 '동전'이 더 자연스럽고, '주화'는 뉴스, 박물관, 화폐 설명 같은 글에서 더 자주 나와요. 짝말은 종이돈인 '지폐'예요.

phrases.en: I have a few coins in my pocket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '주화'보다 '동전'을 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation people use 동전 far more than 주화.

phrases.en: A new commemorative coin for the Olympics has come out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특별한 행사를 기념해서 만든 주화예요. '주화'가 어울리는 대표 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A coin made to mark a special event. This is a typical setting where 주화 fits well.

phrases.example: 옛날 주화를 모으는 게 제 취미예요.
phrases.en: Collecting old coins is my hobby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수집이 취미일 때 쓰는 말로, 외국 주화나 옛 주화를 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for coin collecting as a hobby, fitting for foreign or old coins.

explain_en: In daily life '동전' sounds more natural, while '주화' appears more in news, museums and explanations about currency. Its paired word is '지폐' (paper money).

examples.en: My uncle runs a real estate brokerage business.
You need a license to work in the brokerage business.
Online brokerage businesses have grown a lot these days.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 중고차 중개업으로 크게 성공했어요.
examples.en: That company became very successful in used-car brokerage.
In this brokerage business, trust is the most important thing.
My friend graduated from university and jumped into the brokerage business.

explain: 보통 '부동산 중개업'처럼 사는 사람과 파는 사람 사이에서 거래를 이어 주는 직업이나 사업을 말해요. 일상에서는 '부동산'이라고만 말해도 그런 가게를 가리키는 일이 많아요. 사람을 말할 때는 '중개업자'나 '공인중개사'를 써요.

phrases.en: My father started a brokerage business last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사업이나 일을 새로 시작할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for starting a business or line of work.

phrases.en: I went to a real estate office to look for a house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중개업을 하는 가게를 말하고, 보통 '부동산'이라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The shop that does brokerage; people often just call it 부동산.

phrases.en: Trust is important in the real estate brokerage business.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집이나 땅 거래를 이어 주는 일을 말할 때 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for the business of connecting house or land deals.

explain_en: It refers to the job or business of connecting buyers and sellers in a deal, most often as '부동산 중개업' (real estate brokerage). In daily talk, just saying '부동산' often points to such an office. For the person, use '중개업자' or '공인중개사'.

en: to be increased; to be expanded

examples.en: Cold patients increase in winter.
The number of students has increased a lot this year.

examples.ko: 수입이 증가되면 저금을 더 할 거예요.
examples.en: If my income increases, I will save more.
The company pays the increased cost.
My workload increased, so I am very busy.
There are many regions where the population has not increased.

explain: '늘다'의 글말이라서 숫자나 양이 많아졌다는 보고서와 뉴스에 나와요. 보통은 '증가하다'를 훨씬 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Cold patients increase in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '증가되다'보다 훨씬 자주 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more commonly used than '증가되다'.

phrases.en: The number of tourists is growing a lot these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 숫자나 양이 많아질 때 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easy everyday word for numbers or amounts getting larger.

phrases.en: Sales increased a lot this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '크게'를 붙여 많이 늘었다는 것을 보고할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '크게' is added to report a big increase.

explain_en: It is the written-language counterpart of '늘다' and appears in reports and news about numbers or amounts rising. '증가하다' is used much more often.

dis.h: number or amount goes up, in general

p.n: 신장되다 does not fit numbers of people; it is for power, rights or exports.

examples.ko: 최근 건강에 대한 관심이 크게 증대되었어요.
examples.en: Interest in health has grown greatly lately.
As exports grew, the company's profits increased.

examples.ko: 위험이 증대될수록 더 신중하게 움직여야 해요.
examples.en: The greater the risk grows, the more carefully you must move.

examples.ko: 증대되는 수요에 맞춰 공장을 새로 지었어요.
examples.en: We built a new factory to match the growing demand.

examples.ko: 서비스가 좋아지자 고객 만족도가 증대되고 있어요.
examples.en: As the service improved, customer satisfaction has been rising.

examples.ko: 환경 문제에 대한 책임감이 증대된 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems the sense of responsibility for environmental problems has grown.

explain: 증대되다는 관심·이익·위험·수요처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것이 커질 때 주로 써요. 키나 물건의 크기에는 '자라다', '커지다'를 써요. 숫자가 늘 때는 '증가하다'가 더 흔하고, '증대되다'는 정도나 규모가 커진다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 환경 오염의 위험이 점점 증대되고 있어요.
phrases.en: The risk of environmental pollution is growing more and more.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 커지는 중이라는 변화를 보여 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows a change that is still going on.

phrases.en: My worries are growing these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '증대되다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 두루 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 증대되다 and widely used in daily life.

phrases.en: The number of tourists rises greatly in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 수나 숫자가 늘 때는 '증가하다'가 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: For numbers or counts, 증가하다 is more common.

explain_en: 증대되다 mostly describes intangible things getting bigger, such as interest, profit, risk or demand. For height or physical size, use 자라다 or 커지다. When numbers go up, 증가하다 is more common; 증대되다 stresses the degree or scale growing.

dis.h: formal passive: gets bigger or greater

p.n: Passive versus active form, same meaning here.

t90.ax: Interest in health has grown greatly lately.
